title: Preoperative MELD, MELD‑Na and MELD‑XI Scores as Predictors of Mortality and Morbidity after LVAD Implantation
summary: For patients with end-stage heart failure, the implantation of a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) is an established treatment option; however, it is associated with significant perioperative mortality and morbidity. In addition to cardiac-specific scores, liver function-based scores such as MELD, MELD-Na, and MELD-XI are increasingly being used for preoperative risk stratification, as congestive hepatopathy and renal dysfunction are typical comorbidities of advanced heart failure. The aim of this retrospective study is to investigate the extent to which preoperative MELD, MELD-Na, and MELD-XI scores are associated with short- and medium-term outcomes following LVAD implantation. The study includes all patients who received an LVAD at the Department of Cardiac Surgery at the University Hospital Düsseldorf between 2010 and 2017. MELD, MELD-Na, and MELD-XI scores are calculated from the preoperative laboratory values; patient groups are stratified using predefined thresholds (e.g., MELD <10, 10–19, ≥20, or MELD-XI <17 vs. ≥17).  The primary endpoints are in-hospital mortality and 1-year mortality; secondary endpoints include the duration of intensive care and hospital stays, the need for reoperation, right ventricular failure, and significant bleeding complications. We hypothesize that higher preoperative MELD, MELD-Na, and MELD-XI scores are associated with significantly higher mortality and morbidity and can therefore serve as valid tools for preoperative risk stratification in LVAD patients. The results could help to better identify high-risk patients, adjust perioperative management, and refine the criteria for LVAD implantation.

interventions.name: This retrospective study includes all patients who underwent LVAD implantation at the Department of Cardiac Surgery at the University Hospital Düsseldorf between 2010 and 2017

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All adult patients (aged 18 years or older) who have successfully undergone LVAD implantation (e.g., HeartMate 3, HeartWare HVAD) as a bridge-to-transplant or destination therapy.
Exclusion criteria:
Pediatric cases, temporary RVAD/BiVAD, incomplete laboratory data
